summary: Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Claremont Graduate University, and under Nyanaponika Thera and Balangoda Ananda Maitreya. He was Editor at Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and president of BAUS (2013).

Bhikkhu Pāsādika works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Magadh and Punjabi Universities. He served at Punjabi University (1975–1977), Göttingen Academy (1980–1993), Marburg (1995–2007), Würzburg (1996–2003), Bochum (2000–2003), and Frankfurt Buddhist Academy (2022).
Bhikkhu U Dhammissara is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Sanu Mahatthanadull, attested in 2017.

Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā specializes in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe (attested 2007), and also studied under Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and N. A. Jayawickrama.

Bhogilal Sandesara was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh. He served as Head of the Gujarati Department at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda from circa 1951 to 1975.
Bhuvan Chandel works in philosophy and Indology. She was a professor at Panjab University (~1979–2002) and served as Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1999–2004).

Bhuwan Lal Joshi worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Patna University (~1950–1952) and held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1962–1965) and the University of California, Santa Cruz (~1965–1977).

Bidia Dandaron worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg civil aviation and state universities, and under Lubsan Sandan Tsydenov and Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov. He was a research fellow at IMBT in 1957.

Bimal Krishna Matilal was a philosopher and Indologist. He studied at Calcutta, Sanskrit College, and Harvard under D. H. H. Ingalls. He taught at Toronto (~1968–1977) and was Spalding Professor at Oxford (1977–1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Patna University and SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. His posts included Patna College (~1942–1953), Patna University (1958), and K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1968–1978).
Bing Chen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Sichuan University from circa 1987 and at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences, attested in 1993.
Bingtao Ma is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Peking University (by 2008) and earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xueyu (attested 2015).

Birgit Kellner specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura and with Muni Jambūvijaya. She held posts at the University of Vienna and leads the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Bisheshwar Nath Reu worked in Indology, history, and archaeology, studying under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. He headed the Archaeological Survey of India, Government Museum Jodhpur, Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre, and Sumer Public Library's archaeological department.
Biswanath Banerjee was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University (1967–1991) and served as president of The Asiatic Society (~2004–2007).
Bo Jiang is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who completed a PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2008).

Bo Utas specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University (~1957–1973) under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Stig Wikander, and held a post at Uppsala University from circa 1966 to 2003.
Bo-Kwang Han is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held a professorship at Dongguk University, attested in 2004 and 2015.
Bokar Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1959–1989). He held a post at Bokar Monastery from circa 1984 to 2004.

Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley and earned a PhD at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser, also studying under Jacqueline I. Stone and Lewis Lancaster.
